name: Gliclazide
summary: A second-generation sulfonylurea widely used for type 2 diabetes, available as a once-daily modified-release formulation.
mechanism: Binds the sulfonylurea receptor (SUR1) on pancreatic beta cells, closing ATP-sensitive potassium channels and stimulating calcium-dependent insulin release.
targets: SUR1/Kir6.2 ATP-sensitive potassium channel (pancreatic beta cells)
pharmacodynamics: Improves prandial insulin secretion; may have mild antiplatelet and antioxidant effects (clinical significance uncertain).

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: ~10–12 h (up to ~16 h for modified release)

dosing.adult: Modified release: 30 mg once daily with breakfast, titrate to 60–120 mg once daily; standard release: 80–160 mg/day in divided doses

safety.pregnancy: Not preferred; insulin is standard during pregnancy
warnings: Hypoglycemia, especially with missed meals, alcohol, or renal impairment
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia; treat with oral or IV glucose and close monitoring

indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as adjunct to diet and exercise
Combination therapy with metformin or other agents
clinicalPearls: In the ADVANCE trial it showed microvascular benefit with a low hypoglycemia signal relative to other sulfonylureas.
The MR formulation is dosed once daily, improving adherence.
good: Well-tolerated sulfonylurea with a convenient once-daily MR option and a favorable trial record.
bad: High hypoglycemia risk in the elderly or renally impaired; weight gain.
